selectionRule: Read the matching full article, compare fit and exclusions with the user's requirements, and explain adaptations. This is a starter index, not a fixed list of allowed architectures or proof of compatibility.

architectures.title: Basic Web Application
architectures.fit: Single-region proof of concept or learning application using App Service and SQL Database.
architectures.exclusions: Explicitly not a production baseline. Does not establish private networking, WAF, autoscaling, or zone redundancy.

architectures.title: Baseline Highly Available Zone-Redundant App Services Web Application
architectures.fit: Regional highly available web application needing private dependency access.
architectures.exclusions: Requires supported regions/configuration. Regional redundancy is not multi-region disaster recovery. Ingress and outbound integration have different paths.

architectures.title: Deploy Microservices to Azure Container Apps
architectures.fit: Brownfield microservices migration from Kubernetes with less orchestration management.
architectures.exclusions: Migration compromises are not universal greenfield recommendations. Validate cost, ingress, identity, and message compatibility.

architectures.title: Use a Message Broker and Events to Integrate Enterprise Systems
architectures.fit: Asynchronous integration, burst buffering, unreliable back ends, and long-running workflows.
architectures.exclusions: Queue messages and event notifications are different. Private endpoint and topic support depends on Service Bus tier.

architectures.title: Baseline Microsoft Foundry Chat Reference Architecture
architectures.fit: Network-secured enterprise chat/agent workload with enterprise grounding.
architectures.exclusions: Not proof that every IQ, model family, or Fabric/M365 source plugs into one chain. Validate agent setup, model/tool/region support, state resources, and identity.

architectures.title: Greenfield Lakehouse on Microsoft Fabric
architectures.fit: New batch/streaming analytics platform with OneLake, Spark, data science, and reporting.
architectures.exclusions: Not recommended unchanged for legacy warehouse migration or SQL-focused teams with little Spark expertise. Capacity and permissions are separate decisions.

architectures.title: Hub-Spoke Network Topology in Azure
architectures.fit: Shared regional networking/security, workload isolation, and explicitly required hybrid connectivity.
architectures.exclusions: Customer-managed hub, not Virtual WAN. Peering is nontransitive. Do not add hub/spoke infrastructure to unrelated app or data sketches.

visualReferenceUse: Curated design examples, not model-weight training or a deployment template. Study the matching archetype's visual grammar; do not import its services, regions, or topology into unrelated workloads. Downloaded originals remain separate from the skill ZIP with their source URLs and hashes.
